In total, 66 pupils from HK and Mainland China have studied with us over this period; of these, 6 returned to HK (three entering HK University to read Business or Accountancy and Finance and one went to university in Australia to study Music. The other 59 all went to UK universities with the most popular being Imperial College (8) and UCL (8). With a further three studying at King's College, this made London the most popular university with 19 pupils in total. Nottingham (5) Durham (4) Bristol (3) and Warwick (3) were also popular. Two pupils went to Cambridge. Only 6 pupils went to non-Russell Group universities. Q1.Can you send Mrs Wong and me a prospectus of the school? Mrs Wong would like to know more about the boarding facilities, activities, soft and hardware of the school.
A1. In terms of a précis, I would outline the following:
Kindness and mutual respect are at the very heart of what is expected at Handcross Park. This underlying ethos enables the children to benefit from the outstanding teaching that is available to them. Parents, children and visitors to Handcross Park talk about the warmth and familiarity of the School and that they feel part of a very caring community. Children are encouraged to think for themselves and to develop their own particular interests in a stimulating, structured and flexible environment.
Our facilities are extensive. We have 50 acres of Sussex parkland containing pitches for football, hockey, rugby and cricket. There is a six-hole golf course, a huge athletics area for track and field events and adventure playgrounds. A range of activities are also held in our large, fully-equipped sports hall and heated, indoor swimming pool. Our Music School houses individual practice rooms, together with a large music studio. Each classroom throughout the school is equipped with an interactive smartboard and computer and the Computer Suite, with its twenty work stations, forms only a small part of the whole school intranet.
Our brand new prospectus will be ready to send out next week. We are just awaiting the inserts to be printed outlining fees etc. Would it be acceptable to wait until then?

Q2. Can you provide the ratio of overseas students at Handcross park at the moment?
A2. To date, we have achieved 100% Common Entrance success for our students, feeding some of the top schools in the country. Some of these include; Brighton College, Wellington College, Charterhouse, King’s Canterbury, Lancing, Worth, Ardingly. Many of our students also achieve scholarships to these schools, which have some of the highest academic entrance requirements in the country.
Since our recent merger with Brighton College, we have seen a rise in the number of students who will be attending the school and this will be rising year on year. Next year, we expect to send upwards of 10 children to Brighton College.
Children are required to sit the entrance examinations into the Brighton College senior school and they need to pass these to guarantee a place there. If children do not pass these exams, we work with parents to find another top school for them to attend.

Q3. Can you provide the list that show where the leavers land on after Handcross? How many will be able to enter Brighton successfully?
A3. The ratio of overseas students is approximately 5-10%.

You have chosen to stay with a homestay provider as a paying guest.  You will usually be the only student from your country in the homestay.  This is a valuable opportunity to experience life in a ‘typical’ household, and to hear and speak English outside the classroom.

All our our homestay providers have agreed to abide by the Homestay Code of Practice.  This means that your host will promise:

•	To encourage you to speak English as much as possible in the home
•	To encourage you to feel at home and to treat you as a member of the household rather than a paying guest
•	Not to host another student of the same native language as you at the same time (unless by special agreement with both of you)
•	To provide a clean and comfortable room as recommended by the British Council
•	To provide a home environment you can carry on your English studies properly including use of internet/wireless if they have this facility
•	To provide you with a balanced and appropriate diet
•	To show due concern for your welfare, safety and security during your stay
•	For protection of all members of the household, we ask that doors remain open when alone in a room with a student.
•	To give you reasonable and regular access to bathroom and laundry facilities (some families will do your laundry for you)
•	To communicate regularly with the college and so be in a position to help resolve any problems you may encounter during your stay
•	To respect your different cultural background and be sensitive to your particular needs

The fees for homestay accommodation will be £130 per week for half board (breakfast and evening meal Monday to Friday, three meals Saturday and Sunday) although you may choose to pay for full board only and this can be agreed with your homestay family. If you pay the homestay fees for the year, then the college will issue a cheque to the host family each term.  However, you may prefer to pay the family yourself every four weeks.  There will be a retainer fee payable of £30 per week, payable in advance, when you return home for the holidays.

Some of the homestay families will have children who attend the college, and in other families you will be the youngest member of the household.

If you have any worries about your homestay accommodation you can discuss them with the Admissions Manager at the college.  The relationship with past students and homestay families has been very successful in the past and we are sure you will soon settle in and be made to feel very welcome.

Kingsley – Precautions against the Novel Coronavirus


Dear Parents, Guardians and Agents,

I am writing to let you know what we are doing to keep your children safe and healthy at Kingsley.

We are closely monitoring this complex health situation and we are frequently assessing and updating potential risks to our community. There are now 2 confirmed cases in the UK of the Coronavirus and the World Health Organisation has declared the outbreak a global emergency. Public Health England (PHE) has revised the status of the threat of the virus spreading from low to moderate.

The measures that have been in place at Kingsley since 20th January (16 days), and the professional advice that we are taking daily includes:

·	Daily checks on Public Health England, The Department of Health and Social Care, and with the Medical Officer of Schools Association and advice from the NHS www.nhs.uk/conditions/wuhan-novel-coronavirus .

·	We are in direct daily communication with Public Health England SW 
 
·	We have checked the home addresses of all our Far East pupils, and none are from  Wuhan, the capital of Hubei province and all returned to the UK before the Coronavirus outbreak was announced

-	With half-term looming, we are carefully checking all the travel plans of our international students.  At present, none of our pupils have travel plans to visit China or Hong Kong over half term; if any pupil does visit China or Hong Kong over half term, he/she will not be able to return to Kingsley for at least 14 days after his/her return to the UK. This is a straightforward precautionary measure in line with the best scientific and expert advice on how to stop the Novel Coronavirus from spreading. As more countries succumb to the virus, this list of countries affected by the travel ban/quarantine may be expanded.

-	As usual, Kingsley boarders can remain in school and be looked after by school staff during half term, or they can use this facility should their travel be considered unsafe or be restricted.  Provision to look after international boarders in school during the Easter break is being made so that facility is in place.

·	We will continue to keep pupils informed of the latest advice by the UK and Chinese health authorities, including simple precautionary measures such as proper hand and respiratory hygiene, in their tutor groups and assemblies

·	We are not receiving any visitors to the school from mainland China or Hong Kong (including parents) until the threat from the virus is lifted, or unless they have shared with school details of a medical check in the UK within the last 14 days.

·	Kingsley will also help support pupils who may be anxious about their home country and will support them as best as we can

The wellbeing of our whole school community is our main concern at this time, especially those from China and other affected areas, and I am sure you will join me in supporting them during this worrying period.  While this virus is a very serious global issue, we are reminding pupils to remain calm and not to overreact if anyone in school falls ill as there are always coughs and colds at this time of the year.

Kingsley will continue to follow the latest public health advice and will closely monitor the situation, putting interventions in place, should they be needed. We will continue to keep you informed as the situation and official advice changes. Should you wish to discuss any of the above, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely, 


Mr Pete Last 
Headmaster
Kingsley School Bideford

Of course one area of uncertainty for our international boarders will be international travel and entry requirements for the UK. The government has recently established its ‘traffic light’ system of red, amber and green countries. At present there are very few countries designated as green and therefore the great majority of travellers arriving in the UK currently have to complete a ten day quarantine period on arrival. We hope that this situation may change over the coming weeks and more countries may be added to the green list, but we are planning on the basis that our international pupils will need to quarantine on arrival.

We are pleased to be able to offer all of our new international boarders the option of completing their quarantine period here at School prior to the start of term. We can arrange school transport from Heathrow or Gatwick airports and we have enough space to be able to offer them bedrooms with designated bathroom facilities. Meals and refreshments would be delivered to their rooms and School staff will be responsible for the health and wellbeing of the pupils. The pupils would have daily opportunities to go outside for fresh air and socially distanced exercise.

Any new international pupils wishing to spend their quarantine period here at School would need to arrive on 17, 18 or 19 August to ensure that the quarantine period is completed in time for the start of term. The additional charge for quarantine accommodation is £90 per day and the charge for collection from the airport is £60 for Heathrow and £30 for Gatwick. These charges would be added to your School account. Please note that any pupils arriving in the UK before 17 August or after 19 August will need to complete their quarantine period away from School with their guardians or another responsible adult. If you would like to reserve a place for your child to complete quarantine at school, please contact our admissions department (boardingadmissions@caterhamschool.co.uk) including your child’s name in the subject line of the email.

New Campus in Cambridge:

From 2022 Cardiff Sixth Form College will be opening a second new campus in Cambridge for A Level students.  Cambridge is a natural fit for Cardiff Sixth Form as many of our students go onto study there at University level. As well as 15 subjects and a wide range of extra-curricular activities including sport, music, art, drama and clubs, societies and events, students at Cardiff Sixth Form College will have an extensive supporting curriculum.
